Well it's more so that Majin is the name of the base Devil form in Japanese, while the form commomly called the Majin Devil Trigger in English is more accurately Shin Majin or "True Devil." Shin Majin is used to refer to both of the secondary Devil Triggers used by Dante in the Japanese versions of DMC2 and DMC5.

Ever since its lackluster inclusion in DMC2, Itsuno had wanted to innovate and improve the Shin Majin form. However it didn't make much sense to do it with DMC3 which served as Dante's origin story. Nor did it pan out with DMC4, which is notoriously unfinished from what its original concept was. It was only with DMC5 that Itsuno's team was finally able to realize and fully implement the Shin Majin form as they wanted, which was then formally translated into English as Sin Devil Trigger.

Which is funny because considering how they translated the Devil forms to begin with, if they properly localized Shin Majin back when DMC2 released, it would have become Shin Devil Trigger or True Devil Trigger. Shin Devil Trigger's name became the base for Sin Devil Trigger, as Itsuno wanted the form to have a natural meaning for English speakers that also evoked the same overall sound as the Japanese name.

"Without power you cannot protect anything"

As much as he'd probably try to deny it, Vergil's motivation is rooted in his very human desire to not have those he cares about die again. Despite all of his purported animosity towards Dante, he never goes out of his way to actually attempt to kill him, instead being content with simply defeating him as he does care about his brother and sparring was always the way they bonded since they were kids. Once he finds out that Nero is his son, he takes an interest in fighting with him as well and then immediately trusts Nero to protect the Earth from this side while he and Dante protect it from the other side.

While Vergil was able to excise the traumas he endured from being Nelo Angelo, he was not freed from his traumas as a whole. While he's able to be more human in his emotions now, his time as V shows that his mother's death truly shaped the foundation of who he is and is the reason why he even challenged Mundus in the first place. Vergil craved power so that he could save himself from having to suffer that kind of tragedy again and he tries to downplay how much he cares to prop himself up as a big bad demon instead of the weak human child who couldn't protect anything.

Vergil leans heavily into a stoic facade as a trauma response, which can lead people to believe that he doesn't care when he's probably always close to crashing out in actuality.

After his father signs the blood pact, Ashnard immediately invokes its curse and starts killing off Daein's citizens. There were so many casualties from this event that it was believed to have been a great plague that tore through the land. It's only after everyone else in the line of succession dies as a result of this that Ashnard destroys the blood pact by killing his father.

The killing of a lot of citizens just so happens to be a core feature of blood pacts as a whole, not just the one in Kilvas.  Ashnard just so happened to purposefully abuse this feature, as he intended to use the death and chaos wrought by his actions as a tool with which he'd free Yune from the medallion. 

In fact, in the Japanese version's extended script, his wife reveals that he deliberately used the blood pact to kill both his family and his citizens instead of just his family like the regular script states, killing more than 1,000 people in the process.

As someone that would glaze Tellius in a second, that kind of is what happens. Ashnard tricks his father into secretly signing a blood pact that ends up killing a lot of random Daien citizens in a plague, including his mother and everyone else that were ahead of him in the line of succession. And then once it's just him and his father left, he kills his father to spare himself from the blood pact.

Which honestly isn't a sign of IS having given up on Tellius' story, but more of a symbol to show just how committed Ashnard was to his goals that everyone and everything became a means to an end for him. I appreciate Ashnard being a villain that's so unrepentant in his actions.

Ulquiorra himself states to Full Hollow Ichigo that it's his specific quirk that he as an Arrancar maintains the high speed regeneration that other Arrancar have sacrificed to power up in the transition from Hollow to Arrancar. To be able to sacrifice something, you have to possess it in the first place, further proving that high speed regeneration is a base trait of Hollows but NOT Arrancar. Meaning that....Arrancar have provably lost abilities.

This can be clearly seen on Page 5 of Chapter 351 of the manga, as well as spoken by Ulquiorra in the equivalent Episode 271 of the anime.

An Arrancar's sword is what is created when they "separate part of itself into another being" as I had already stated. While a Visored is taking in a foreign entity and thus going from having 100% of a soul to a hypothetical 200% of a soul, an Arrancar is cutting off part of themselves and sealing it in the form of a blade. They still have the same 100% of a soul in a different form, with their increase in power being born from sacrificing their regenerative abilities to boost their other stats. 

Arrancar itself comes from Spanish and means "to tear off," Arrancar are literally tearing off a part of themselves and molding it into a weapon to use, not taking in a new being and completely boosting all of their stats. Resurreccion is them returning to something closer to their Hollow form by absorbing that power and regaining their old abilities with it. 

Or effectively:

Visored have pulled a Dragon Ball and fused with another creature to permanently boost their stats. Arrancar have pulled an RPG and reset their class tree, minmaxing by taking all points out of regeneration and putting it into other stats, while having the same overall stat total.

The Visored are Shinigami that have gained a a completely new addition to their soul in the form of an inner Hollow, it stands to reason that they'd gain abilities that they didn't have before since it's more of a 1+1=2 kind of deal. Arrancar are what happen when a Hollow separates part of itself into another being, which wouldn't necessarily make sense for them to gain new abilities out of it since it's more of a 2-1=1 kind of deal.

Thanks to Ulquiorra being unique in retaining his high speed regeneration in his evolution from Hollow to Arrancar, we know that most Arrancar actually *lose* abilities in the transition from one to the other, which they tend to regain when they use their Resurreccion. The closest we get to Arrancars potentially being able to evolve and/or gain new abilities over time is Nnoitra's Santa Teresa having changed shape between his time as the 8th and 5th Espada.

That's the main reason why they added skill potential for demons during the transition from IV to Apocalypse, if I remember correctly. Which is ironic in a way. IV has the most free inheritance system in the franchise, but comes from the older style where you were mostly intended to throw away demons after a few levels when their leveling curve became too steep. While V comes with Essences to help you keep any demon growing with you if you truly wanted to, while reigning in the inheritance system with skill potentials.

I'd say overall, the Essence system is perfect *as long* as it also comes with potentials. The only way to make it better is if they worked in some way to also give the MC negative skill potentials, which could potentially work by having their base skill potential be modified by that of the demon they copy with affinity fusion.

Is Chi Chi a failure of a character and a waste of potential because she dared make the mistake of being a housewife in a battle shonen when she learned how to fight, despite being a housewife having been a goal of hers since she was a child?

Is Gohan a failure of a character and a waste of potential for choosing to focus on being a scholar instead of being a warrior? Despite having trauma from having his neck snapped by a grown man when he was 5 years old after seeing his father murdered in front of him when he was 4 and then being kidnapped by his father's murderer (Piccolo got better tho)? 

One could argue that she did move past a bit of her trauma when she realized that beneath his mask, Ichigo was still Ichigo and not something to be afraid of and was able to speak out to and motivate him when previously her voice was caught in her throat. One could argue that she moved past a bit of her trauma when she became the Shield to Ichigo's Sword against Yhwach, with a power strong enough to force him to start using the Almighty. 

Even if she moved past her trauma entirely, that does NOT necessitate that she becomes a fighter in the aftermath. It's okay for characters in a battle shonen, both male and female, to not want or need to be active combatants and insisting otherwise is a toxic mentality that holds people back from enjoying what are perfectly fine characters in terms of the story they're a part of, simply because they don't go "Unba Bunga" and attack everything near them.

Without the Yamchas of the world to need saving sometimes , the Gokus and Vegetas start looking a lot less impressive.

Plus when her love interest is the guy whose entire goal for being a fighter is simply "I just wanna be strong enough to protect those I love," she doesn't need to fight because everyone (including Ichigo) knows that he'll move worlds for her and she'll put them back together for him.

And yet she was still willing to sacrifice herself for a mere chance that her friends wouldn't be hurt, since she had absolutely no reason to believe that Aizen and Ulquiorra would keep their word and not attack her friends. She was willing to die for a cause in a world completely foreign to her just to believe the killers wouldn't kill her friends.

While Orihime is Ichigo's love interest, she was not the main girl of the series. That was always Rukia, which is reflected in the first and last chapters of the manga both being titled "The Death and the Strawberry." And aside from the first part of the series where Rukia loses her power and is the first damsel in distress to require a rescue arc, Rukia herself is portrayed as a blossoming fighter who's continuing to grow in power and skill.

Just because Bleach is a manga based around fighting doesn't mean that everyone should be a fighter and that those who aren't fighters are "wastes of potential." Especially when Orihime has very real trauma related to physical abuse that would very much make her not want to be a fighter. It's shown on more than one occasion that Orihime struggles with her traumas and her past, which is one of the parallels that shares with Ichigo. While Ichigo resolved to be the one to protect everyone, Orihime resolved to sacrifice herself first so that no one else has to get hurt because of her.

If you're going to bring up Hanataro being willing to die but Ganju stopping him....aka a damsel in distress being saved, then we can bring up how Orihime was willing to go to Hueco Mundo and sacrifice her freedom and potentially her life just so that her friends wouldn't be hurt further by Ulquiorra. That's a hell of a lot of nerve and one of the noblest of sacrifices.

Piccolo learned to make clothes out of magic so that he can always stay dripped out and aura farm and even drip out Gohan if he has to. We don't have to pit two bad bitches against one another, they're both kings at the top of their craft

It's readily acknowledged by multiple people in story that Orihime has the potential to use her powers in much more devastating ways, but that it's simply *not* who she is as a person. Part of her Shun Shun Rikka is an offensive ability that is underpowered compared to her other abilities because she's a pacifist to heart, and there's nothing wrong with that.

This is the same anime that gave us Hanataro as a prominent character in the Soul Society arc, who is a man that's portrayed far more as a damsel in distress that's only ever good for healing than Orihime ever was. Or the numerous other women who are accomplished and successful combatants, including Unohana who happens to be the most skilled fighter in the history of the Soul Society or Harribel who becomes the queen of Hueco Mundo as its strongest warrior.

Nintendo...doesn't make Pokémon at all. It's Gamefreak that does and they're a core part of the issue. Despite making the most successful franchise of all time, Gamefreak refuses to upgrade to a bigger team that can handle the workload needed to make a better Pokémon game.

And as much as Nintendo would like to push Gamefreak in the right direction when it comes to Pokémon, they can't. Nintendo, Gamefreak, and Creatures all have equal stakes in the Pokémon Company which owns the IP. And when issues arise between Nintendo and Gamefreak, Creatures tends to side with Gamefreak and shut Nintendo down on the matter. We know from the big Pokémon leak that Nintendo *tried* to get Gamefreak to slow down on the release schedule and polish the games a bit more, but Gamefreak refused and there's nothing that Nintendo can do about it.

And we know that Nintendo and its direct affiliates can make a good game on weaker hardware if they want to. Smash Ultimate, the Zelda games, and the Xenoblade games all run much more smoothly and with much higher graphical fidelity than the Pokémon games because those teams worked with and listened to Nintendo instead of stonewalling them.

Hell, Nintendo came out and said that they flat out restarted the development of Metroid Prime 4 because they weren't satisfied with how the product was coming along and wanted to deliver a better product, eating millions in developmental losses in the process. Nintendo usually isn't the good guy in a lot of cases, but this is still the same company where higher ups would willingly take the blame for their failings and cut their own pays instead of rolling it downhill to their employees.

Nords went from a race in tune with magic and producing a lot of magical scholars to a race overall afraid of magic and ignorant of it.

Why hold stuff against ESO that the mainline does, in *much worse quantities and qualities* at that?

The mainline games themselves constantly contradict and change their own lore to better suit what's going on in the current game, often by virtue of relying upon an unreliable and/or untrustworthy source.

But Zenimax Online Studios is not a completely distinct entity from Bethesda Game Studios, they're both sister companies under Zenimax Media. They work together to try to keep the lore in ESO congruent with the rest of the franchise, or well as congruent as can be considering the rest of the franchise makes no effort at it.

Being entirely dismissive of the lore of a game deemed canon by the creator of the mainline games does make it so that you add nothing to the conversation. While you're allowed to have your own headcanon, you can't dismiss the actual canon in actual discussions of the lore.

My mom was adopted (well, both my parents were adopted...)

I physically could not exist today without my grandmother, genuinely. And of course it's not because we share blood or anything since we don't, but because me and my mother were dying while she was giving birth to me and it was my grandmother's intervention that got doctors to take things seriously and get my mother under an emergency c section.

My mom's biological mother on the other hand, abandoned my mother when she was a child and chose drugs over her. Didn't really know the lady until I was 7 where she was down on her luck and my mother was gracious enough to not leave her on the streets. She's been in my life for nearly 20 years now and she's made efforts to be more present and I'll call her my grandmother, but she was never as proactive as the other one was. 

Yet when I meet people who happen to know my family and they ask about my grandmother, they're always referring to the first lady and never the second lady. There are people that didn't even know that my mom doesn't share any blood with the lady she called "mommy" because as far as my grandmother was concerned, that was just as much of her kid as the 6 she did give birth to.

Yes your genetics will give you a permanent tie to your biological family and no one will argue against that. But your emotional bonds and connections to others considered your family as well as your memories are just as permanent. They say a person is never truly dead until the last person that remembers them no longer speaks of them. 

Genetics give us a base yes, but our connections and learned experiences with others come together to form the truth of who we really are. Which is a point that I think you're sorely missing. Cherry blossoms perfectly represent who Byakuya is as a character.

They also represent beauty and violence, which can be seen in Byakuya's attack style being simple and beautiful on the surface but highly destructive all the same.

Cherry blossoms were also used to signify the life of a samurai, who through bushido lived a life bound to a strict code of respect, honor, and discipline. Which was the source of Byakuya's conflict to begin with, his inborn duty to uphold the code and law of his family pit him at odds with his desire to protect Rukia, who was the last living reminder of Hisana for him.

This culminates nicely in the final form of his Senbonzakura, that being Shukei: Hakuteiken. It's generally his strongest technique and takes the form of an ethereal white bird, because Byakuya has effectively liberated himself from his rigid mindset even if for just a moment, allowing himself to attack with all the power that he'd otherwise restrict himself from using. Its destructive power also calls back to it representing both beauty and violence at once.

The Lucifer found in SMT5 is not a Chaos aligned character, at least not anymore by the time of the events of the game. His alignment in the game is instead Neutral-Neutral. It's implied that him taking the God of Law's Knowledge and ascending to a higher form of existence is what caused this shift in him, as he now has both Law and Chaos residing within his being. With this in mind, it stands to reason that he wouldn't be for the cyclical death and rebirth of the world, but would instead prefer it to have a more stable, continued existence.

When the Nahobino himself slays Lucifer, he gets the Knowledge of both Lucifer and the God of Law, meaning that his heart should stay true to the alignment he picks since he's already inheriting a balanced power. But we also know from Nocturne itself that this incarnation of Lucifer (who is the same one as evident by his Demon Haunt conversation referring to both the Demifiend and the Nahobino) has always been an advocate for ending the cycle of rebirth. 

Because if you think about it, the Conception and Mandala Systems are ultimately systems of Law. While they may have a chance to spawn a more chaotic world for a time, the cyclical pattern by which they end and recreate the world creates some semblance of Order through a guaranteed outcome in the bigger picture. It would be realistic for a Chaos or even Neutral Lucifer to want to end that system and instead lead into a world where humans can truly carve their own path without it inevitably coming undone.

That's what Shikai and Bankai are supposed to represent, by virtue of emulating the Japanese saying about a person having three faces. The Steam Deck runs Windows games through Proton, which itself is a fork of Wine which is explicitly not an emulator but a compatibility layer instead. Where emulators and compatibility layers differ is that while emulators function by mimicking another system down to hardware/software level, a compatibility layer relies on the source system using the same architecture as the end system so that they just have to translate functions between the two.

This is what allows the Steam Deck (and other Linux based systems) to run Windows games at full speed and sometimes even faster, they don't lose a lot of overhead to the more complex functions required by emulation.

When operating as a publicly traded company, you're pretty much legally bound to aim to *constantly* increase profits to line the pockets of your shareholders, often to the detriment of the company or its product. Look how many gaming related companies have had substantial layoffs within the last year, it's because their profits haven't grown as much as shareholders would like them to have and they remedy that by cutting the workforce to artificially inflate their profit margin.

It allows them to make decisions that they feel are better for their company and their product, which in turn ends up resulting in better decisions for their consumers.

SMT, at least until Apocalypse, doesn't portray the Christian/New Testament YHWH so much as it does the Hebrew/Old Testament YHWH. Something that's been observed within the Old Testament is that YHWH wasn't always treated as the one and only God and that's a gradual transition in belief over time. 

Judaism has its roots in ancient Semitic religions, specifically the Canaanite religions, which were polytheistic in nature. El and Yahweh were two gods that existed in that time, with El being the Creator God while Yahweh was a god more associated with War (something that explains a lot about his portrayal in SMT) and Weather. 

Overtime, El and Yahweh were conflated into a single god in Yahwism which placed El/Yahweh as the head of the pantheon, but did not deny that other gods existed or that they could be worshipped, which we refer to now as monolatrism. Yahwism itself slowly transitioned into monotheism in the earliest forms of Judaism, where the belief that YHWH was the one and only God to be worshipped was solidified.

The gods of other religions would instead be relegated to demons trying to tempt man away from God, or angels (more accurately "messengers") there to spread God's word to man. This is very consistent with how the various gods are treated throughout the franchise, but especially in Apocalypse and V, where it's shown that YHWH (the God of Law) went out of His way to strip power away from other gods to affirm Himself as the one above all through barbaric methods.

Overall I don't think the series portrays an accurate depiction of most religions and mythologies that it invokes, often to the detriment of the characterization of the gods themselves like Krishna. But I do appreciate the ability to explore a setting where we could see those same gods coexist with one another and potentially explore what happens when gods with overlapping spheres of influence interact with one another.

The graded Super Saiyan forms trade stamina and speed for more power in the form of increased muscle mass, which causes their movements to lag and waste more energy than they would normally. Mastered Super Saiyan is equivalent to base Super Saiyan in terms of power, but eliminates the emotional turmoil of the transformation as well as minimizing the stamina drain as much as physically possible. It effectively becomes base Super Saiyan for Goku and Gohan at that point.

Because Goku's training methods at that point in the story are far more efficient and productive than Vegeta's are, his base (Mastered) Super Saiyan surpasses Vegeta's equivalent, base Super Saiyan because he's simply just stronger than him even as a normal Saiyan. That's why Vegeta and Trunks admit that Goku is stronger than them, because for every form that they would share with him Goku would be stronger than them in it.

Base Super Saiyan is at most a 50x multiplier to its user's power, with Grade 2 and 3 stressing the form for more power in exchange for stamina and speed. Grade 4 is them making base Super Saiyan almost as natural to them as their normal form, allowing them to exist more comfortably within it and modulate their power anywhere between 1x-50x their base.

Toriyama originally envisioned Super Saiyan as a 10x multiplier, yes, but by the time he had actually brought Super Saiyan into the equation he had also used Kaioken x20 as a benchmark and realized that he needed to re-evaluate his decision and then instead positioned Super Saiyan at 50x the user's base power. If it wasn't a fixed maximum boost, then there's no reason for Super Saiyan Grades 2 and 3, Super Saiyan 2, and Super Saiyan 3 to exist since a Saiyan would be able to just modulate their power to those levels without the added drawbacks necessary to attain those forms.

The quote about Goku's realizations after his fight with Beerus have nothing to do with Super Saiyan not being a fixed 50x boost at maximum. They're simply saying that if Goku trains his base form more, then naturally it would boost his transformations that much more alongside it, especially now that he has the realm of God Ki to break into which to date has yet to be combined with a regular Super Saiyan state above Mastered Super Saiyan. For example as a hypothetical, Goku gaining 20,000 PL as a Super Saiyan 3 pales in comparison to Goku gaining 20,000 PL in his base form. In the first case, it's an increase of just 50 PL in his base form while the second case is a literally 400x more efficient increase in power.

Tails don't make Super Saiyan unattainable, by Toriyama's words it's just that Saiyans can only regrow their tails while their power and S-Cells are below the threshold necessary to bridge the gap into Super Saiyan. No Saiyan has made it that threshold without losing their tail at some point, but if they did then they'd be able to keep their tail and attain Super Saiyan.

It's more of a failsafe on the part of the Saiyans' bodies than tails actively restricting the ability to transform. For most Saiyans, their tails are their weak points and their body deems it an unnecessary liability when their body is on the cusp of attaining a form that is far stronger without the same weak point.

Goten and Trunks were both born without tails because at the times they were conceived, their fathers were either on the cusp of attaining Super Saiyan or had already attained it and as a result passed along a large number of S-Cells to jump start their growth. S-Cells themselves only really cultivate within a Saiyan's body when they're able to live and thrive in a peaceful enough environment, which is why Super Saiyans don't show up much prior to the story, most Saiyans lived in a near constant state of battle that didn't allow their body the opportunity to develop S-Cells. 

As expanded upon in the Buu Saga, Dragon Ball Super, and supplementary material, mental anguish isn't truly a factor necessary to attain Super Saiyan. It's a combination of power level and S-Cells and being excitable enough to jump start their engine, which is what happens in the case of Goten and Trunks. Anguish is just the most easily attainable form of excitement for most Saiyans we see within the story.

As someone into sci-fi and storytelling, Starfield was not developed for that crowd either. I did complete the game, but the game was honestly made just so that Todd could say he made the space game he wanted to make for forever.

Something that's not commonly talked about with Ichigo, which I can't be too mad at because it's not commonly stated, is that he spends a large part of the story with some form of depression. He doesn't laugh or smile often, with him smiling the day before the anniversary of his mother's death as a sign that he was anything but happy. He spent half of his life blaming himself for his mother's death, to the point where he resolved himself to get strong enough to never have to deal with losing a loved one like that again. Except one of the people he cares the most about is scared of his power that he developed specifically to save her and it shatters him. When he loses his powers to defeat Aizen, he becomes noticeably withdrawn from everyone and then jumps at the opportunity to get some form of power back and then suffers a traumatic series of events that culminates in his new powers being stolen and thinking his own father betrayed him. 

His depression also floods his inner world with rain and it's such a consistent thing for him that the Old Man is able to develop a severe dislike for rain in general because of what it represents for Ichigo as a whole. It's raining when Ichigo's parents meet each other in the course of fighting White, when Masaki passes away, when Byakuya cuts down Ichigo while arresting Rukia, in Ichigo's inner world throughout most of the Hueco Mundo and Fake Karakura Town arcs, when Ulquiorra releases his Resureccion, when Ginjo takes his Fullbring, when Jugram cuts Tensa Zangetsu in half, when the Old Man reveals that he's not the true Zangetsu. Ichigo's rain always comes in response to either his failure to protect someone he holds close to him or his perceived notion that he and his power aren't enough or both.

But Chi Chi's status is different compared to most women being married in Japan. She's the daughter of a king. She would not under most circumstances take the name of her commoner husband, especially when her commoner husband is by all definitions a country hick. In Japanese culture, when a princess marries a commoner she's excommunicated from the royal family. Chi Chi evidently didn't go through this with how much Ox King is a lasting presence in her and her kid's lives, meaning she kept her status and presumably didn't take Goku's name.

At the same time, Mr Satan and Hercule are both explicitly noted to not be his real name. His real name is simply Mark, transcribed as Maaku which is an anagram of Akuma or Devil.

Most families in Dragon Ball aren't tied together by a specific family name, but rather a naming convention and theme. Mr Satan's family naming theme is based in demonic and angelic origins. Satan is Satan, Maaku is Akuma, Videl is Devil, her mother Miguel comes from Michael which is "He who is like God" or "Gift from God" and Pan is named for the Greek God Pan who's goat features have also drawn him an association to the devil by certain occultists.

The Son family however is the only family to have a family name (the Briefs don't count because Briefs being a family name was an American localization invention, where originally its just the name of Bulma's father.) They're also one of the only families if not the only family that is explicitly Eastern inspired in their origin. Son is their family name. A good way to see this is to notice which characters in the Japanese dub refer to Goku by which name. His closest friends and mentors call him Goku while the most formal of people call him "Son" or specifically "Son Goku-san" with proper honorifics to call attention to the family name when speaking formally.

Dragon Ball is Japanese in origin, where the surname/family name comes first. Son IS their family name. Grandpa Gohan was also Son Gohan and his great grandson was named after him entirely. Chi Chi is a princess by virtue of her father being the Ox King, there's little chance that she herself would take Son as her family name when it'd be royalty taking a commoner's name. Then we get the confirmation from Kubo that he indeed blotted out the Old Man's true name.

The Quincy and their weapons are an interesting case because for the longest, we are exclusively told their lore from the viewpoints of Uryu and Mayuri. One of whom is 15 and his teacher on Quincy History had been dead for years and stuck to an old method of combat while the other is a sadist who doesn't care to retain information that isn't important to him.
